ei.title: The Need to Let Go of the Stress in Your Mind
ei.subject: 6월_2022 고1 모의고사
ei.lesson: The Need to Let Go of the Stress in Your Mind

fullPassage: A psychology professor raised a glass of water while teaching stress management principles to her students, and asked them, "How heavy is this glass of water I'm holding?" Students shouted out various answers. The professor replied, "The absolute weight of this glass doesn't matter. It depends on how long I hold it. If I hold it for a minute, it's quite light. But, if I hold it for a day straight, it will cause severe pain in my arm, forcing me to drop the glass to the floor. In each case, the weight of the glass is the same, but the longer I hold it, the heavier it feels to me." As the class nodded their heads in agreement, she continued, "Your stresses in life are like this glass of water. If you still feel the weight of yesterday's stress, it's a strong sign that it's time to put the glass down."

questions.passage: A psychology professor raised a glass of water while teaching stress management principles to her students, and asked them, "How heavy is this glass of water I'm holding?" Students shouted out (A)[various / identical] answers. The professor replied, "The (B)[absolute / relative] weight of this glass doesn't matter. It depends on how long I hold it. If I hold it for a minute, it's quite light. But, if I hold it for a day straight, it will cause (C)[severe / mild] pain in my arm, forcing me to drop the glass to the floor. In each case, the weight of the glass is the same, but the longer I hold it, the heavier it feels to me." As the class nodded their heads in agreement, she continued, "Your stresses in life are like this glass of water. If you still feel the weight of yesterday's stress, it's a strong sign that it's time to put the glass down."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
① relative: 절대적 무게라고 했으므로 부적절
② various — absolute — severe ←정답
③ identical: 다양한 답을 외쳤다고 했으므로 부적절
④ mild: 심한 통증이라고 했으므로 부적절
det.tip: 학생들의 반응, 무게의 성질, 통증의 정도를 파악하세요.

questions.passage: A psychology professor raised a glass of water while teaching stress management principles to her students, and asked them, "How heavy is this glass of water I'm holding?" Students shouted out various answers. The professor replied, "The absolute weight of this glass doesn't matter. It depends on how long I hold it. If I hold it for a minute, it's quite light. But, if I hold it for a day straight, it will cause severe pain in my arm, (A)[forcing / allowing] me to drop the glass to the floor. In each case, the weight of the glass is the same, but the longer I hold it, the heavier it feels to me." As the class nodded their heads in (B)[agreement / disagreement], she continued, "Your (C)[stresses / pleasures] in life are like this glass of water. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
① allowing: 팔이 아파서 강제로 떨어뜨리게 한다는 맥락이므로 부적절
② disagreement: 고개를 끄덕이며 동의했다는 맥락이므로 부적절
③ pleasures: 스트레스가 물잔과 같다는 맥락이므로 부적절
④ forcing — agreement — stresses ←정답
det.tip: 통증으로 인한 결과, 학생들의 반응, 비유의 대상을 파악하세요.

questions.passage: A psychology professor raised a glass of water while teaching stress management principles to her students, and asked them, "How heavy is this glass of water I'm holding?" ③ lighter: 오래 들수록 더 무겁게 느껴진다고 했으므로 부적절
④ excuse: 내려놓을 때라는 강한 신호라는 맥락이므로 부적절
det.tip: 무게의 속성, 시간에 따른 변화, 결론의 의미를 파악하세요.

det.analysis:

det.tip: 하루 종일 물잔을 들면 어떤 종류의 통증이 생기는지 파악하세요.

questions.passage:
(A) A psychology professor raised a glass of water while teaching stress management principles to her students, and asked them, "How heavy is this <u>glass</u> of water I'm holding?"

(B) She looked through the <u>glass</u> window and noticed the students gathering in the hallway before the lecture began.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 glass의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
① (A) 유리: glass of water에서 잔의 의미

③ (A) 잔 — (B) 유리 ←정답: (A)는 물잔, (B)는 유리창
④ (A)(B) 둘 다 유리: (A)는 잔의 의미
det.tip: glass는 '잔'과 '유리' 등 다양한 뜻이 있습니다.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "very bad or serious; causing great pain or suffering"

② absolute: 절대적인은 정도를 나타내는 다른 의미
③ various: 다양한은 종류를 나타내는 단어
④ straight: 곧장/쭉은 방향이나 시간을 나타내는 단어
det.tip: 'great pain or suffering'에 주목하세요.

det.analysis: 분사 전환: 주절 동사(will cause)의 결과를 나타내는 분사구문. force → forcing (현재분사).
det.tip: 콤마 뒤에서 동시 동작이나 결과를 나타내는 분사구문입니다.
